name: Vicious Night Web Spider Venom
summary: In eastern Tirisfal, Vicious Night Web Spider Venom carries an old contagion. The Royal Apothecary Society prizes it for holding historical disease strains, and uses it in work on the Forsaken's New Plague.

sections.title: A Preserved Contagion
sections.body: Apothecary Johaan in Brill studies old texts about a plague that killed thousands. The contagion behind that outbreak endured for centuries inside the venom of local Night Web spiders. Apothecaries hunt the vicious breed in Venomweb Vale, south of the Scarlet Monastery, and draw out the preserved contagion for their alchemical experiments.

sections.title: Fueling the New Plague
sections.body: The Forsaken seek a weapon against the Scourge and the living. Johaan adds the venom as the final component of his experimental concoction, hoping its preserved contagion will work with the mixture.

faq.q: What makes this venom unique compared to regular spider poison?
faq.answer: Old texts studied by the Royal Apothecary Society tell of an ancient plague pathogen preserved in the venom glands of the Night Web spider lineage. Their poison holds a reservoir of contagion.

faq.q: Where can the spiders carrying this venom be found?
faq.answer: Vicious night web spiders live mainly in Venomweb Vale, in eastern Tirisfal Glades south of the Scarlet Monastery.

faq.q: Who wants this venom in Brill?
faq.answer: Apothecary Johaan in Brill wants multiple samples to continue his research into a new infectious agent for the Forsaken.

faq.q: How does the venom fit into the Forsaken's research?
faq.answer: Johaan needs the venom as the final component of his experiment. Old texts describe an ancient plague preserved in Night Web Spider venom, and he wants to learn whether its contagion will work with his concoction.

angles.text: As Forsaken, gathering this venom helps Lady Sylvanas pursue her mandate to develop a plague powerful enough to bring down Arthas and his Scourge.
As a Rogue familiar with natural neurotoxins, you can see how the Royal Apothecary Society turns dangerous wild venoms into engineered bio-weapons.
